core.title: Keep user/system flow sequences strictly linear; model new paths as new user/system flows
core.given: You are planning a user/system flow
core.when: you author or change any user/system flow sequence (e.g. adding steps, or when the flow seems to need a loop, a route, a branch or an alternative path)
core.then: Keep the user/system flow's sequence strictly linear (steps only, no loops, routes or branching) and express every new path as a new user/system flow.
prefer: Model each new or alternative path as its own new linear user/system flow instead of a loop, route or branch inside the existing sequence
Number steps sequentially with no gaps (1, 2, 3, …)
Give every step exactly one from and exactly one to
avoid: Adding loop or route sequence elements to a user/system flow
Encoding branching through a step with multiple from/to targets
Leaving gaps in step numbering after inserting or removing steps
core.why: Linearity is the no-loops/no-routes/no-branching rule for user/system flow sequences: sequences contain steps only, and new paths MUST become new user/system flows rather than variations inside one sequence.
evidence: The user/system flow sequence contains only step elements — no loop or route elements
Step numbers are contiguous with no gaps
Each step has exactly one from and exactly one to
Any new or alternative path introduced by the plan exists as its own new user/system flow
verification: The check enforces three constraints on every user/system flow sequence: loop and route sequence elements are forbidden; sequential step numbering must have no gaps; each step has exactly one from and one to.

User/system flow specification files are identifiable as plan artifacts of the user/system-flow-specification kind in the plan tree, which is why the file-kind fact is observable now; the rule fixes no recognition mechanism of its own.

Observing the 'change' facts (a user/system flow sequence added or modified, a sequence element other than a step added, step numbering changed, a step's from/to changed) requires a diff-level parser of the user/system flow sequence; without such an observer, only the file-kind, operation and task-term facts are observable.

What the check does not decide on its own: whether a planned flow introduces a loop/route construct, branching, or a new/alternative path that must become a new user/system flow is a design judgement; steps written out explicitly one after another in a linear sequence are not by themselves a finding.

Scope of the check: user/system flow specifications only. Edits to user/system flow metadata outside the sequence (title, description) without touching steps, and plan artifacts that are not user/system flows, are out of scope.

values: user/system flow sequence added or modified
sequence element other than a step added

fires: Planner authors a new user/system flow, including an ordinary linear step sequence (numbering and from/to cardinality still apply)
Planner creates a new user/system flow to carry an alternative path split out of another user/system flow
Planner inserts, removes or reorders steps in an existing user/system flow
Planner adds a loop or route element to a user/system flow sequence
Planner models an alternative/error path inside an existing user/system flow instead of a new user/system flow
User/system flow steps are renumbered leaving a gap (e.g. step 1, 2, 4)
A step declares more than one from or more than one to, or omits one
doesNotFire: Editing user/system flow metadata outside the sequence (title, description) without touching steps
Planning artifacts that are not user/system flows (e.g. product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES, acceptances) with no user/system flow sequence change

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role; the core's 'user/system flow specification' file kind must be among them so the file-kind activation fact can be observed.

classification.note: Neutral: the user/system flow is a cross-stack plan artifact; no stack, path or suffix named.
Kept verbatim; user/system-flow-spec vocabulary, not stack idioms.
Constraint stated generically in core.verification[0]; no detector/validator/finding ids are declared.
The 'linearity' term definition is identical to the core why.
Neutral file-kind fact kept in the core; its recognition note is carried generically in core.verification[1]; the concrete kind value comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds.

neutralityNotes: The rule governs a plan artifact and the Bun sidecar names no stack, runtime, language, suffix or path, so the core is essentially verbatim and bunOnly is empty. User/system flow, step, loop/route, from/to and sibling plan artifacts (product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance) are neutral ATDD plan vocabulary (the closed vocabulary lists them as cross-stack urn artifacts). Round 4 fixes: the stack name was removed from core.verification[1]; the roles.plan_artifact.kinds bunValue is now the exact string value 'user/system flow specification'. Recognition mechanics (role assignment, plan path, plan-artifact suffixes) are not populated by the Bun sidecar, so no values are invented for them. No per-rule disposition is declared in the Bun sidecar, so none is invented.
